描述_ZN: Fan Style Monument", also known as "Fan Juqing Monument". It was erected in the first month of the third year of the Qinglong period (235) of the Three Kingdoms. The full text of the stele is recorded in Song Hong Shi's "The Interpretation of the Official Script", with 19 lines and 33 characters. The name of the stele is inscribed in four columns, 10 lines in the first and second columns, 11 lines in the third column, and 6 lines in the fourth column. The frontal seal script reads "The monument of Fan Fujun, the former governor of Lujiang" in 10 characters.　　The monument was originally located in Rencheng, Shandong Province, but was later moved to Jining Prefecture. After the Song Dynasty, the monument was broken and lost in the earth. In the forty-first year of Qianlong of Qing Dynasty (1776), Cui of Jiaozhou first got the remnants of the tablet in the water mouth of West Longmen Square of Jining State School, and Li Dongqi and Huang Yi carved the trek under the tablet. Qianlong fifty-two years (1787), Li Dongqi regained the original monument remnants in the state school palace under the halberd door, Huang Yi, Li Kezheng and carved trek in the monument yin. The stone is now stored in the Han monument group of Tieta Temple in Jining.　　The Fanshibi Monument is one of the famous monuments of the Three Kingdoms of Wei. The calligraphy of this stele retains many characteristics of the Eastern Han Dynasty official script. Li Dongqi wrote: "The stone is very ancient and I was surprised that it was a Han monument. When I wiped it, there were several names of people in clerical script. I dug and washed it, and it was the Fan Shih Stele."　　This is the Song topography of the stone in Huang Yi's collection before it was unearthed, and the inscription has more than 180 characters than the topography after it was unearthed. The paper and ink are antique and the characters are sufficient. Each page is 34 cm in length and 17 cm in width. The back panel is inscribed with Lu Wenshao and Weng Fanggang, and there are 34 Tibetan seals such as "Weng Fanggang" and "Qu Zhongsol".　　It is recorded in Zhao Mingcheng's "Jinshilu" in the Song Dynasty, Weng Fanggang's "Jinshilu of the Two Han Dynasties" in the Qing Dynasty, and Wang Chang's "Jinshilu Zuiji".
